stem: A new marketing hire needs an account today. Your org has no identity-provider integration and this is a one-off. What is the fastest correct way to create the account?

choices.text: Set up SAML SSO with a third-party IdP
Manually create the user in the Admin console
Import the user with Google Takeout

explain: For a single, one-off account with no external source, manual creation is correct. GCDS and SAML are for ongoing or federated provisioning; Takeout is an export tool, not a creation tool.

stem: You're onboarding 250 employees from an acquired company. You have a CSV of their details and no directory to sync from. What is the best approach?

choices.text: Bulk-upload the users from the CSV
Deploy GCDS against the acquired company's old AD

explain: Bulk CSV upload is designed for tens-to-hundreds of accounts from a spreadsheet when there is no live source to sync.

stem: Your company authenticates everyone through Microsoft Entra ID in the cloud and wants accounts provisioned into Workspace automatically, without running an on-prem server. Which tool fits?
explain: Directory Sync is the Google-hosted sync from a cloud IdP such as Entra ID — no server to run. GCDS requires an on-prem connector; DMS migrates data, not accounts.

stem: An employee is leaving and their My Drive files must stay available to their manager. What should you do FIRST?

choices.text: Transfer Drive ownership to the manager
Suspend then immediately delete the account
Export the files to your own account with Takeout

explain: Transfer ownership before any deletion; deleting first can destroy My Drive data. Once transferred, you can safely delete or suspend.

stem: You deleted a user 10 days ago and now need the account and its data back. What can you do?

choices.text: Restore the user from Deleted users (within the 20-day window)
Recreate the user; data returns automatically
Open a Vault matter to rebuild the account

explain: A deleted user can be restored within 20 days. Recreating a same-name account does not bring back data, and Vault is not a recovery tool for deleted accounts.

stem: A support team needs one address that several agents monitor, where incoming requests can be assigned and tracked among them. Which group type?
explain: A Collaborative Inbox is a shared mailbox that lets members assign, track, and resolve incoming messages — ideal for support@.

stem: You want a group whose membership always includes everyone whose department attribute equals “Sales,” updating automatically as people join or leave. Which group type?
explain: Dynamic groups derive membership from a query on user attributes and update automatically. (The attribute must actually be populated on users.)

stem: Your company acquired newco.com and wants every existing user to also receive mail at name@newco.com — without creating any new accounts. What do you configure?

choices.text: A user alias for each person individually

explain: A domain alias gives all existing users a matching address on the new domain automatically. A secondary domain hosts a separate set of accounts.

stem: After adding and verifying a secondary domain, its users still cannot receive external email. What did you most likely miss?

choices.text: Adding MX records for the secondary domain

explain: Verification proves ownership, but mail only flows once the domain's MX records point to Google. The symptom — no inbound external mail — points to missing MX records. Section 2 · Managing core Workspace services (~23%)

stem: External recipients report that mail from your domain frequently lands in their spam folders. Which action best addresses the root cause?

choices.text: Ask each recipient to allowlist your domain
Ensure SPF, DKIM, and DMARC are all correctly configured
Increase the Gmail attachment size limit
Disable Security Sandbox to speed up delivery

explain: Outbound mail being spam-foldered is almost always an email-authentication gap. Completing the SPF + DKIM + DMARC trio is the durable fix; recipient allowlists don't scale.

stem: You must ensure that any external message containing the phrase “Project Halo” is held for an administrator to review before it leaves the organization. What do you configure?

choices.text: A Gmail content compliance rule that quarantines matching mail

explain: Content compliance rules inspect message content and can route matches to an admin quarantine for review before delivery.

stem: An executive wants their assistant to read and send email from the executive's mailbox without knowing the password. What do you enable?
explain: Gmail delegation grants another user access to read and send mail on the owner's behalf, with no password sharing.

stem: Which statement about Shared Drives is correct?

choices.text: Files are owned by the individual who created them
Files must be transferred whenever a member leaves
Files are owned by the team and remain when a member leaves
Shared Drive files count only against an individual's storage quota

explain: Shared Drive content belongs to the team, so it persists through off-boarding — a key reason to use Shared Drives for organizational content.

stem: Your org wants to remove the blunt “anyone in the organization” sharing suggestion and instead present a curated set of sharing scopes to users. What do you configure?
explain: Target audiences let you define named scopes that replace the broad “anyone at <org>” default in the share dialog.

stem: Only the Marketing team should be able to share Drive files with a specific partner domain; no other department should. Which is the most precise control?

choices.text: A Drive trust rule scoped to the Marketing OU and the partner domain
A DLP rule blocking all external sharing

explain: Trust rules give granular, directional sharing control by OU/group/domain — exactly this department-to-specific-domain requirement.

stem: You're moving mailboxes from an on-prem Microsoft Exchange server into Gmail. Which tool is built for this?
explain: The Data Migration Service migrates mail/calendar/contacts from sources like Exchange. The sync tools handle accounts, not data migration.

stem: A team needs Meet recordings and transcripts available for their meetings. Where do you enable these?

choices.text: Google Meet video settings in the Admin console, per OU

explain: Recording, transcripts and related video features are controlled in the Meet settings in the Admin console and can be scoped per OU (edition permitting).

stem: Leadership worries that using Gemini will expose company data to model training. What is the accurate reassurance?

choices.text: Gemini cannot access company data at all
Enterprise data isn't used to train Google's models and stays within the tenant's protections
You must disable Gemini entirely to stay safe
Data is shared only with verified third parties

explain: Enterprise prompts and content are not used to train Google's models and remain within the organization's protections.

stem: A department head wants a no-code app built from a Google Sheet to track equipment loans, with no developers involved. What do you recommend?
explain: AppSheet is Google's no-code platform for building apps/automations from Sheets and Drive data. Apps Script requires writing code. Section 3 · Managing data governance & compliance (~15%)

stem: Legal places a litigation hold on a user whose Gmail is otherwise set to auto-delete after 12 months. What happens to messages older than 12 months?

choices.text: They are purged on schedule — retention always wins
They are preserved because a hold overrides retention deletion
They are exported to the admin automatically
They are moved to Trash for 30 days

explain: A Vault hold always overrides a retention rule's deletion. Held data is preserved until the hold is removed — the single most-tested Vault fact.

stem: A former employee's mailbox must be retained for seven years for compliance, but you don't want to pay for a full user license. What do you use?

choices.text: A standard license plus a Vault hold
A Takeout export saved to Drive

explain: An Archived User License retains a departed user's data in Vault without consuming a full active seat.

stem: A user emptied their Trash and now needs back a Doc they deleted yesterday. What is the correct recovery path?

choices.text: Have an admin restore the user's recently deleted Drive data within the recovery window
It is gone immediately and unrecoverable
Rebuild it from a Shared Drive

explain: Vault is for retention/eDiscovery, not backup. An admin can restore a user's recently deleted Drive/Gmail data within the limited recovery window.

stem: You must block external sharing of files that contain credit-card numbers, while only warning users in less-sensitive cases. Which feature?

choices.text: DLP rules with content detectors and actions

explain: DLP combines detectors (e.g. credit-card numbers) with graduated actions (block, warn, audit) across supported services.

stem: Which Workspace services can DLP rules be applied to?
explain: DLP supports Gmail, Drive, and Chat (with differing capabilities per service).

stem: A regulated client requires that covered data be stored at rest in Europe. What do you configure?

choices.text: A secondary domain hosted in the EU
A Vault export location in Europe
A Drive trust rule for EU users

explain: Data regions control where covered data is stored at rest. A Vault export location only affects where exports are produced.

stem: You need a one-time export of the entire organization's data for a legal review. Which tool is appropriate (and restricted to Super Admins)?
explain: The Data Export tool performs a whole-organization export and is restricted to Super Admins under specific conditions. Takeout is per-user self-export. Section 4 · Managing security policies & access controls (~20%)

stem: The board mandates that Workspace be reachable only from corporate-managed devices, regardless of who is signing in. Which control fits best?

choices.text: Configure Context-Aware Access with a device-based access level

explain: The requirement is conditional on device state — exactly what Context-Aware Access expresses. 2SV verifies identity (not context), DLP governs data, and a VPN is a network control.

stem: You are enabling 2-Step Verification enforcement organization-wide. What must you configure to avoid locking out users who haven't yet registered a second factor?

choices.text: An enrollment (grace) period before enforcement begins

explain: Always allow an enrollment grace period (and a new-user enrollment window) so people can register a factor before enforcement takes effect.

stem: Which 2SV methods are the most phishing-resistant? (Choose TWO)
explain: Security keys and passkeys are phishing-resistant. SMS is the weakest 2SV method; backup codes are a fallback, not phishing-resistant primary factors.

stem: A new help-desk hire should reset user passwords but must not change security settings or billing. Which prebuilt role follows least privilege?
explain: Help Desk Admin is deliberately limited to password resets and basic user help — the least-privilege fit.

stem: You want to review, at a glance, whether sharing and authentication settings across Gmail, Drive, and Calendar follow best practices. Where do you look?

choices.text: The security dashboard / security health page

explain: The security dashboard and health page give an overview of posture and flag configuration gaps. The investigation tool is for searching and remediating specific incidents.

stem: A phishing email reached 200 inboxes. You must locate every copy and delete it from users' mailboxes. Which tool?
explain: The investigation tool can search across mailboxes and take remediation actions such as deleting messages and suspending users.

stem: A risky third-party app is requesting broad OAuth access to users' Gmail and Drive. How do you prevent this organization-wide?

choices.text: Rely on the Marketplace allowlist alone
Use API controls to mark the app Blocked and restrict access to sensitive scopes

explain: API controls (OAuth app access) let you classify apps as Trusted/Limited/Blocked and restrict access to sensitive Gmail/Drive scopes.

stem: Users sign in on shared kiosk machines and should be signed out automatically after a short period. What do you configure?
explain: Google Session Control sets how long web sessions last before re-authentication — ideal for shared devices.

stem: Which are Google-recommended practices for Super Admin accounts? (Choose TWO)

choices.text: Use them for routine daily administration
Keep the number of Super Admins small
Protect them with the strongest 2SV, such as security keys
Share one Super Admin account across the team

explain: Limit how many Super Admins exist and protect them with the strongest 2SV. Don't use them for daily work, and never share accounts. Section 5 · Managing browsers & endpoints (~10%)

stem: An employee leaves and returns their personal phone, which held the corporate account. You must remove company data but leave their personal content untouched. What do you do?

choices.text: Block the device from the network

explain: For BYOD, an account wipe removes only corporate data. A full device wipe is appropriate for company-owned hardware.

stem: Your org wants to require screen locks and be able to wipe corporate data from personal phones with minimal setup and no agent installed. Which management level?
explain: Basic mobile management is agentless, on by default, and supports screen-lock enforcement and account wipe.

stem: You need device approval and full device wipe on company-owned phones. Which management level (edition permitting)?
explain: Advanced mobile management provides device approval, stronger policies, app management, and full device wipe.

stem: You must force-install a specific Chrome extension for the Finance OU only. Where do you do this?

choices.text: Devices > Chrome > Apps & extensions, scoped to the Finance OU

explain: Chrome extension policies (force-install / allow / block) are set under Devices > Chrome > Apps & extensions and scoped by OU or group.

stem: Before you can apply Chrome browser policies centrally, what must you do first?

choices.text: Enroll the browsers using an enrollment token

explain: Browsers must be enrolled (via an enrollment token) into Chrome Browser Cloud Management before policies apply. Section 6 · Monitoring & troubleshooting (~13%)

stem: Multiple users report Gmail is down. What is your first check to see whether it is a Google-side outage?
explain: The Status Dashboard shows known service disruptions — the right first stop for an “is it down for everyone?” question.

stem: A user says an email they expected two days ago never arrived. What is the most direct tool to trace its delivery?
explain: Email Log Search traces a specific message's delivery path and status within the last 30 days.

stem: An email failed authentication and you want to inspect its SPF/DKIM/DMARC results from the raw header. Which tool?
explain: The Messageheader tool in the Admin Toolbox (toolbox.googleapps.com) parses a raw header and shows authentication results.

stem: Google Support asks for a network capture of a failing web request in Chrome. What do you provide?

choices.text: A HAR file captured from Chrome DevTools

explain: A HAR file (DevTools > Network > Preserve log > reproduce > Save all as HAR) captures the network exchange. Treat it as sensitive.

stem: Users complain of poor audio and video quality in Meet calls. Which tool helps diagnose network/quality issues?
explain: The Meet quality tool surfaces network and media-quality data to diagnose A/V problems.

stem: You need to find out who changed a Drive sharing setting in the Admin console last week. Which log?

choices.text: The Drive log eventsDrive log events
Email Log Search Additional practice questions (Q47–Q246)

explain: Administrative setting changes are recorded in the admin audit log. (The Drive log shows file/sharing activity by users, not admin-console setting changes.) Additional answer key & explanations (Q47–Q246) Section 1 · Managing user accounts, domains & Directory (~20%)

stem: An employee is going on a six-month sabbatical and will return to the same role. You want to block sign-in and preserve their mailbox without deleting anything. What should you do?

choices.text: Delete the account and recreate it later
Reset the password and hide it
Move the account to a disabled OU

explain: Suspending blocks sign-in while keeping all data and the license intact, so the account can be restored instantly on return. Deletion risks data loss; an OU move doesn’t stop sign-in.

stem: A user is locked out and cannot reach their recovery options. As an admin with the right role, what is the most direct way to get them back in?

choices.text: Reset the user’s password in the Admin console

explain: An admin can reset a user’s password directly in the Admin console and optionally require a change at next sign-in. Recreating the account would destroy their data.

stem: You reset a user’s password and want to make sure they choose their own the next time they sign in. What do you enable?

choices.text: Force password change at next sign-in

explain: The “require password change at next sign-in” option forces the user to set a new password, so the temporary one you set isn’t kept.

stem: Your company runs an on-premises Active Directory and wants to sync users and groups into Workspace using a connector you host yourself. Which tool fits?
explain: GCDS is the self-hosted connector that synchronizes from on-prem LDAP/Active Directory. Directory Sync is the Google-hosted option for cloud IdPs.

stem: You need to create 30 new organizational units and 600 users for a new division quickly and consistently. What is the best approach?

choices.text: Use a bulk CSV upload for users and create the OU structure to match
Create everything by hand in the console
Use Google Takeout to import them

explain: Bulk CSV upload handles hundreds of accounts efficiently, and OUs can be built to receive them. Manual creation at that scale is slow and error-prone.

stem: A setting is configured at the top-level organization but the Sales sub-OU needs a different value. What happens when you set the value on the Sales OU?

choices.text: The change is rejected; child OUs always inherit
The Sales OU overrides the inherited value for its users
All OUs change to the new value

explain: Child OUs inherit by default but can override a parent’s setting locally, which is the basis of OU-based policy targeting.

stem: You want a group you can use as a security principal to grant access to apps and resources, not just to distribute email. Which group type do you create?
explain: Security groups can be used to control access to services and resources. A plain distribution list is for email delivery only.

stem: A user changed their legal surname. You update their primary email to match. By default, what happens to their previous address?

choices.text: It is kept as an alias so old mail still arrives

explain: When you rename a user, Google keeps the former address as an alias so messages sent to the old name continue to be delivered.

stem: You want everyone whose title contains “Manager” to automatically belong to a group that updates as titles change. Which group type?
explain: Dynamic groups derive membership from a query over user attributes and keep membership current automatically.

stem: Facilities asks you to register 12 meeting rooms across three floors so staff can book them in Calendar. What’s the most efficient way to add them?

choices.text: Create each room as a user account
Create buildings and add rooms in bulk under Buildings and resources
Create a Shared Drive per room
Add each room as a group

explain: Rooms are managed as resources under Buildings and resources and can be created in bulk; they’re not user accounts or Shared Drives.

stem: A bookable lab should only be reservable by the Research team. What do you configure?

choices.text: Resource booking permissions restricting who can book it

explain: Booking permissions on the resource control which users or groups may reserve it.

stem: You need staff to see which rooms have a whiteboard and are wheelchair accessible when booking. How do you surface this?

choices.text: Rename each room with the details
Create a separate calendar per feature
Put it in a Drive label
Add resource features such as “whiteboard” and “wheelchair accessible”

explain: Resource features add searchable attributes (capacity, equipment, accessibility) that appear when users browse rooms.

stem: An employee who left three months ago must have their email retained for compliance, but you don’t want to pay for an active seat. What do you use?

choices.text: Keep a full license and suspend them
A Vault export saved to your Drive

explain: An Archived User license retains a former user’s data for Vault retention/eDiscovery without consuming a standard seat.

stem: You want each new user placed into the right OU to automatically receive the correct license without manual assignment. What feature handles this?
explain: Automatic licensing assigns a product license to users based on their OU, removing the need to assign each one by hand.

stem: You must hand a departing employee’s My Drive files to their manager and then delete the account. What is the correct order?

choices.text: Delete the account, then ask Google to recover the files
Transfer Drive ownership to the manager first, then delete
Suspend, then delete with no transfer

explain: Always transfer ownership before deletion; deleting first can permanently remove My Drive data.

stem: You add a new secondary domain and need to prove you own it before activating services. Which DNS record verifies ownership?
explain: Domain verification uses a TXT or CNAME token in DNS; MX records control mail routing, which comes after verification.

stem: Your firm acquired the brand shop-now.com and wants every existing user to also receive mail as name@shop-now.com with no new accounts. What do you add?

choices.text: A per-user alias one at a time

explain: A domain alias mirrors every existing address onto the new domain automatically; a secondary domain hosts a separate set of accounts.

stem: A new subsidiary needs its own set of user accounts under a different domain within the same Workspace account. What do you configure?
explain: A secondary domain hosts distinct accounts (user@second-domain.com) within the same Workspace, unlike an alias which only duplicates addresses.

stem: A user needs two extra addresses (sales@ and info@) routed to their existing mailbox. What’s the simplest setup?

choices.text: Add user aliases to the existing account

explain: User aliases route additional addresses to one mailbox without new accounts or licenses.

stem: You suspended a user two weeks ago. Does that free up their license?

choices.text: No, a suspended user still consumes their license

explain: Suspended accounts continue to consume a license; to free a seat you must delete the account or move it to an archived license.

stem: A user was deleted 12 days ago and you need the account and data back. What can you do?

choices.text: Restore the user from Deleted users within the recovery window
Recreate the same name and data returns
Open a Vault matter to rebuild it

explain: A recently deleted user can be restored (typically within 20 days), bringing back the account and its data.

stem: You want to provision and deprovision users automatically based on your cloud identity provider so that disabling someone in the IdP removes their Workspace access. Which capability handles this?

choices.text: Automated user provisioning/deprovisioning via the IdP (e.g., Directory Sync or SCIM)

explain: Federated provisioning from the IdP (Directory Sync or SCIM-based) automates creating and removing accounts in step with the source of truth.

stem: You are configuring SAML SSO so users authenticate at a third-party IdP. In this flow, what role does Google Workspace play?
explain: In SAML SSO with a third-party IdP, Workspace is the service provider that trusts assertions from the IdP.

stem: Support wants a single address, helpdesk@, that several agents share to receive, assign, and resolve tickets among themselves. Which group type?
explain: A Collaborative Inbox lets members take, assign, and resolve conversations sent to one shared address.

stem: You want a simple email-forwarding list so messages to all-staff@ reach everyone, with no assignment or access-control needs. Which is most appropriate?

choices.text: A distribution list (group used for email)
A dynamic security group with conditions

explain: A standard distribution list/group is the lightweight choice for fan-out email delivery without ticketing or access control.

stem: You’re designing the OU structure. Which approach follows Google-recommended practice?

choices.text: Mirror the structure to how you need to apply different policies, keeping it as simple as possible
A separate OU per individual user
Match OUs exactly to email aliases

explain: Design OUs around policy differences and keep the hierarchy simple; over-nesting and per-user OUs add needless complexity.

stem: A migration project will move mail and calendar from a previous Google Workspace account into yours. Which tool is intended for moving the data?
explain: The Data Migration Service migrates mail, calendar, and contacts from supported sources, including another Workspace account.

stem: A new hire reports they can sign in but have no Gmail, Drive, or Calendar. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: No Workspace license is assigned to the account

explain: Without an assigned license the user has an account but no access to the licensed services.

stem: You need to add a building so rooms can be organized by location and capacity reporting works correctly. Where do you start?

choices.text: Create the building first under Buildings and resources, then add rooms to it
Create a group named after the building

explain: Buildings are the container for rooms; create the building, then add rooms with capacity and features beneath it.

stem: You want to move 40 users from the Contractors OU to the Employees OU to apply employee policies. What’s the cleanest method?

choices.text: Delete and recreate them in the new OU
Select the users and move them to the Employees OU (bulk move)
Create aliases in the new OU

explain: Moving users between OUs (individually or in bulk) reassigns the policies that apply; deletion is unnecessary and destructive.

stem: Leadership wants you to keep the number of people who can change critical settings to a minimum while still delegating routine work. Which is the best practice?

choices.text: Grant least-privilege prebuilt/custom roles and keep Super Admins few

explain: Least privilege — delegate scoped roles and keep Super Admin membership small — limits risk while enabling delegation.

stem: You want to monitor whether users have weak passwords across the organization. Where do you look?

choices.text: The password monitoring/strength view in the Admin console

explain: The Admin console surfaces password strength/length so you can identify and remediate weak passwords.

stem: You need to enforce a minimum password length and prevent password reuse for all users. Where is this set?

choices.text: The organization’s password policy in Security settings

explain: Password length, strength, and reuse constraints are configured in the password management policy under Security.

stem: You want a group whose settings (who can post, who can view members) you can manage centrally and apply consistently. What lets you apply settings to the group?

choices.text: Group access settings in Groups for Business / Admin console

explain: Group settings control posting, joining, and visibility; these are managed in the Groups settings for the organization.

stem: An admin asks how to give a single user three different email addresses that all land in one inbox without extra licenses. What do you recommend?

choices.text: Three user aliases on the one account

explain: Multiple user aliases on one account deliver several addresses to the same mailbox at no extra license cost.

stem: After verifying a newly added secondary domain, its users still receive no external mail. What is the most likely missing step?

choices.text: Publishing MX records that point the secondary domain’s mail to Google

explain: Verification proves ownership, but inbound mail only flows once the domain’s MX records point to Google.

stem: You want resources like company cars and AV kits to be bookable alongside rooms. How are these represented?

choices.text: As resources (non-room resources) under Buildings and resources

explain: Equipment and other bookable items are created as resources, the same place rooms live, and become bookable in Calendar.

stem: You restored a deleted user, but their group memberships and some settings did not all return. What is the best expectation to set?

choices.text: Restoration always returns 100% of every configuration
Core account and data return, but some memberships/settings may need to be reapplied

explain: Restore brings back the account and primary data within the window, but certain group memberships or settings may need reapplying.

stem: A team wants a shared mailbox where they can also see message status (assigned, resolved) for accountability. Which feature provides that?
explain: Collaborative Inbox adds assignment and status tracking on top of a shared group address.

stem: HR sends you a spreadsheet to update job titles and departments for 400 existing users at once. What’s the most efficient method?

choices.text: Use a bulk update via CSV (or the Directory API) to apply the attribute changes

explain: Bulk attribute changes for many existing users are best done via CSV upload or the Directory API rather than one at a time. Section 2 · Managing core Workspace services (~23%)

stem: Legal requires a standard confidentiality notice appended to every outbound external email. What do you configure?

choices.text: An organization-wide compliance footer (append text) rule

explain: A compliance footer (append-text) rule adds a standard disclaimer to outbound mail organization-wide.

stem: You must stop users from sending or receiving executable .exe attachments. Which Gmail control fits?

choices.text: Block the file type via attachment/compliance settings

explain: Gmail can block specific attachment types (or quarantine them) using attachment compliance/blocked file-type settings.

stem: Your security team runs an on-prem filtering appliance and wants all inbound mail to pass through it before Gmail. What do you configure?
explain: An inbound gateway tells Gmail that mail arrives via your gateway, so spam handling and IP allowlisting work correctly.

stem: A trusted partner’s legitimate bulk mail keeps getting marked as spam. What’s the appropriate fix?

choices.text: Add the partner’s domain/IP to an allowlist (approved senders)

explain: Allowlisting the partner’s domain or IP keeps their wanted mail out of spam without disabling protection globally.

stem: You want messages that match a content rule to be held for an administrator’s review before delivery. What do you set up?

choices.text: A content compliance rule that routes matches to quarantine

explain: Content compliance rules can quarantine matching messages so an admin approves or rejects them before delivery.

stem: To let receiving servers cryptographically verify your mail isn’t forged, which record do you generate in the Admin console and publish in DNS?
explain: You generate a DKIM key in Gmail settings and publish the matching DNS TXT record so recipients can verify the signature.

stem: Your mail is delivered but spoofed lookalikes are reaching partners. You want to tell receivers to quarantine or reject unauthenticated mail from your domain. Which record?

choices.text: A DMARC record with a policy (quarantine/reject)

explain: DMARC publishes a policy telling receivers how to handle mail failing SPF/DKIM alignment, reducing spoofing.

stem: You are moving mailboxes from a hosted IMAP provider into Gmail. Which tool is designed for this data move?
explain: The Data Migration Service supports IMAP-based mail migration into Gmail.

stem: For a sensitive OU, new Drive files should default to internal-only, with no external link sharing unless explicitly changed. What do you configure?

choices.text: Set the default sharing/external sharing options for that OU to internal

explain: Drive sharing settings let you set the default and restrict external sharing per OU.

stem: A project team’s documents must remain with the team even as members come and go. Where should the files live?

choices.text: A Shared Drive owned by the team
A personal folder shared with everyone

explain: Shared Drive content is owned by the team, so it persists through membership changes.

stem: You need to cap how much storage the Interns OU can consume each. What do you set?

choices.text: A storage limit/quota for the OU

explain: Storage quotas can be applied to OUs (or users) to cap consumption.

stem: Security wants to prevent the Finance OU from installing Drive for desktop. Where do you control this?

choices.text: The Drive for desktop (sync clients) setting scoped to the Finance OU

explain: Allowing or disallowing Drive for desktop is a Drive setting you can scope per OU.

stem: You want users to be able to tag documents with classifications like “Confidential” that can later drive DLP. Which Drive feature?
explain: Drive Labels let users (or admins) classify files; labels can be referenced by DLP and search.

stem: Field staff need to open and edit Docs without connectivity. What do you enable?
explain: Enabling offline access lets users work in supported editors without a connection and sync later.

stem: Marketing wants every new proposal to start from an approved, branded layout available in the template gallery. What do you set up?

choices.text: Custom Docs templates in the organization’s template gallery

explain: Custom templates published to the org template gallery give users approved starting points.

stem: A shared lab calendar should auto-accept bookings only when the room is free and decline conflicts. What do you configure?
explain: Resource booking policies control auto-accept and conflict handling for room/equipment calendars.

stem: An executive wants their assistant to manage their Calendar — create and edit events on their behalf. What do you enable?

choices.text: Calendar delegation (Make changes and manage sharing / make changes to events)

explain: Calendar delegation grants another user rights to manage the owner’s calendar and events.

stem: By default, internal users should be able to see each other’s free/busy but not event details. What setting controls this?

choices.text: The default internal calendar sharing option (free/busy vs full details)

explain: The default internal sharing option sets whether colleagues see free/busy only or full event details.

stem: Leadership wants to stop users from sharing full calendar details with people outside the organization. Where do you set this?

choices.text: External calendar sharing options (limit to free/busy or none)

explain: External sharing options for Calendar limit what (if anything) external parties can see.

stem: Users complain about spam meeting invites from strangers cluttering their calendars. What setting helps?

choices.text: Turn on “only show invitations from known senders” / prevent invitations from unknown senders

explain: Calendar can be set so invitations from unknown senders don’t automatically clutter the calendar.

stem: An event’s organizer is leaving the company and the recurring meeting must continue under a new owner. What do you do?

choices.text: Transfer event ownership to another user

explain: Transferring event ownership keeps the meeting and its settings under a continuing owner.

stem: A team needs Meet recordings saved automatically for later review. Where do recordings land, and where do you enable it?

choices.text: In Gmail; enabled in mail settings
In Drive; enabled in Meet video settings (per OU)
In Vault only; enabled in Vault
In Chat; enabled in Chat settings

explain: Recording is enabled in Meet video settings (scoped per OU) and recordings are stored in Drive.

stem: For a school OU, students should not be able to start or rejoin meetings without a teacher and shouldn’t see certain controls. Which Meet area applies?
explain: Meet safety settings govern host controls, who can join/rejoin, and related protections for an OU.

stem: You must turn Meet off entirely for the Contractors OU while leaving it on elsewhere. How?

choices.text: Disable Meet for the Contractors OU

explain: Services like Meet can be enabled or disabled per OU, so you scope the off-state to Contractors.

stem: You want Chat conversation history off by default but allow users to turn it on. Which setting?
explain: Chat history can be defaulted on or off, and you can allow users to change it per conversation/space.

stem: A space needs to include people from a partner domain. What must be enabled?
explain: Allowing outside domains in Chat lets external users join spaces, subject to your settings.

stem: You want to add an approved ticketing bot into Chat for your help desk. What do you do?

choices.text: Add/allow the Chat app (bot) for the organization or OU

explain: Chat apps/bots are added and allowed through Chat app settings for the org or specific OUs.

stem: Leadership worries Gemini for Workspace will use company prompts to train Google’s models. What is the accurate reassurance?

choices.text: Gemini can’t access any company data
You must disable Gemini to be safe
Data is shared with verified third parties
Enterprise content and prompts aren’t used to train Google’s models and stay within your protections

explain: Workspace gen-AI content and prompts aren’t used to train the foundation models and remain within the tenant’s protections.

stem: You want to pilot Gemini with only the Innovation OU before a wider rollout. How?

choices.text: Enable Gemini for the Innovation OU only

explain: Gemini can be enabled or disabled per OU, which is ideal for a scoped pilot.

stem: Leadership asks for evidence of how much Gemini is being used across teams. What do you produce?
explain: Gemini usage reports summarize adoption and activity for the organization.

stem: A department head wants a no-code app built from a Google Sheet to track equipment loans, with no developers. What do you recommend?
explain: AppSheet builds apps and automations from Sheets/Drive data without writing code; Apps Script requires coding.

stem: A team needs a custom automation with complex logic and calls to other Google APIs, written in code by a developer. Which platform fits?
explain: Apps Script is the code-based platform for custom automation and API integrations across Workspace.

stem: A legacy desktop client needs to fetch mail over a standard protocol. Which Gmail access setting might you enable for that OU?
explain: POP/IMAP access lets legacy clients connect to Gmail; enable it where required (and consider security trade-offs).

stem: To reduce data exfiltration risk, leadership wants to stop users from automatically forwarding their mail to outside addresses. What do you change?

choices.text: Disable automatic forwarding in Gmail settings for the OU

explain: Disabling automatic forwarding prevents users from auto-routing mail to external addresses.

stem: Users need to share files larger than Gmail’s attachment limit. What’s the recommended approach?

choices.text: Raise the SMTP limit beyond 25 MB
Share via a Google Drive link instead of attaching

explain: Gmail caps attachment size; large files should be shared as Drive links, which Gmail offers automatically.

stem: Compliance wants a blind copy of all outbound external mail sent to a monitoring mailbox. What do you configure?

choices.text: A content compliance/routing rule that also delivers a copy to the compliance address

explain: Content compliance and routing rules can add a recipient (e.g., a compliance archive) to matching messages.

stem: You want to replace the broad “anyone in <org>” option in the Drive share dialog with curated scopes users can pick. What do you configure?
explain: Target audiences define named sharing scopes that appear in place of the broad organization-wide suggestion.

stem: Only the Marketing OU should be allowed to share Drive files with one specific partner domain; no other team may. What’s the most precise control?

choices.text: A Drive trust rule scoped to Marketing and that partner domain

explain: Trust rules give directional, scoped control — exactly a department-to-specific-domain requirement.

stem: On a Shared Drive, which role can add and remove members and change settings?
explain: The Manager role can add/remove members, change settings, and delete content; lower roles cannot manage membership.

stem: A team wants Meet to automatically generate meeting notes and a transcript. Where is this controlled?

choices.text: Meet video settings (transcripts/notes), per OU and edition permitting

explain: Transcripts and automatic notes are governed by Meet video settings, subject to OU scope and edition.

stem: You want Chat spaces allowed but one-to-one direct messages disabled for an OU. Where do you configure Chat behavior?

choices.text: Chat settings in the Admin console (scoped per OU)

explain: Chat behaviors (spaces, history, external access, and related options) are configured in Chat settings per OU.

stem: You want to let users use Gemini’s connection to Workspace apps (e.g., pulling from Gmail/Drive) in the Gemini app. What must you enable?

choices.text: Google Workspace extensions for the Gemini app

explain: Enabling Workspace extensions lets the Gemini app access connected Workspace apps for the user.

stem: Mail to a small partner must always route through a specific path you define, separate from normal delivery. Which Gmail capability handles custom routing?
explain: Gmail routing settings let you define how mail to/from particular senders or recipients is delivered.

stem: You need to transfer ownership of a specific folder and its files from one user to another within the organization. What’s a supported method?

choices.text: Only the user can do it; admins cannot help
Use the admin Drive ownership transfer (or have the user transfer) to the new owner

explain: Ownership of files/folders can be transferred to another user (by the owner, or via admin transfer for departing users).

stem: A user reports they can’t enable offline Docs even though you turned the policy on. What’s a common requirement they’re missing?

choices.text: Using a supported browser with the offline extension/setting enabled on that device

explain: Offline access also depends on the user enabling it in a supported browser/profile on the specific device.

stem: You need to ensure spam handling behaves correctly even though all inbound mail first hits your security gateway. Besides the inbound gateway setting, what should you also do?

choices.text: Identify the gateway IPs so Gmail trusts them and applies spam settings to the original sender

explain: Listing the gateway IPs lets Gmail evaluate the true originating sender for spam, rather than treating the gateway as the sender. Section 3 · Managing data governance & compliance (~15%)

stem: Legal places a hold on a user whose Gmail is set to auto-delete after 12 months. What happens to messages older than 12 months?

choices.text: They’re purged on schedule — retention always wins
They’re exported to the admin automatically
They’re preserved because a hold overrides retention-based deletion

explain: A Vault hold always overrides retention deletion; held data is preserved until the hold is removed.

stem: You want Gmail messages automatically deleted after three years organization-wide unless a hold applies. What do you create in Vault?

choices.text: A retention rule that deletes after the set period

explain: Retention rules automatically retain and then delete data after the configured period (holds take precedence).

stem: You need different retention for the Finance OU than the rest of the company. What do you configure?

choices.text: A custom retention rule scoped to the Finance OU

explain: Custom retention rules can target specific OUs/services with different durations than the default.

stem: Counsel needs to search a custodian’s mail and Drive and produce results for litigation. Which tool?
explain: Vault provides eDiscovery search and export across supported services for legal matters.

stem: Your organization must ensure Vault exports are produced in a specific geographic location. What do you configure?

choices.text: A secondary domain in that region

explain: Vault lets you choose the export location to meet jurisdictional requirements.

stem: Compliance wants periodic reports of who accessed Vault and what searches/exports were run. What do you use?
explain: Vault audit reports track user activity within Vault, including searches and exports.

stem: A regulation requires retaining a departed contractor’s data for seven years without paying for an active seat. What’s the right combination?

choices.text: Apply an Archived User license plus a retention rule/hold
Suspend indefinitely on a full license

explain: An Archived User license retains the data in Vault economically; retention/holds enforce the seven-year requirement.

stem: You must block external sharing of files containing credit-card numbers while only warning users on lower-sensitivity matches. Which feature?

choices.text: DLP rules with content detectors and graduated actions

explain: DLP pairs detectors (e.g., credit-card numbers) with actions like block or warn across supported services.

stem: You need to detect an internal account-number format that no built-in detector matches. What do you use in a DLP rule?

choices.text: A custom detector using a regular expression (and optional match thresholds)

explain: DLP supports custom detectors via regular expressions for organization-specific patterns.

stem: Which Workspace services can DLP rules apply to?

choices.text: Gmail, Drive, and Chat (capabilities differ per service)

explain: DLP covers Gmail, Drive, and Chat, though available conditions/actions vary by service.

stem: When a user’s share is blocked by DLP, you want them to see a clear, branded explanation. What do you configure?
explain: DLP rules support customizable user notifications explaining why an action was blocked or warned.

stem: Only the Legal OU may share Drive files with outside-counsel.com; all other external sharing for them stays blocked. Which feature is most precise?

choices.text: A Drive trust rule limiting Legal’s sharing to that one domain

explain: Trust rules give scoped, directional control to allow only specific OU-to-domain sharing.

stem: You want to block any external sharing of files from the R&D OU regardless of recipient. Which control best expresses this?

choices.text: A trust rule blocking external sharing for the R&D OU

explain: Trust rules can block sharing outside the organization for a specific OU.

stem: A partner needs to view a shared file without a Google account, but leadership wants to control such access. What concept applies?

choices.text: Visitor sharing / external-user controls in trust and sharing rules

explain: Visitor sharing lets non-Google users access shared content via PIN; trust/sharing rules control whether it’s allowed.

stem: You want to stop users in the Sensitive OU from exporting their own data with Takeout. What do you change?

choices.text: Turn off Google Takeout (or specific data types) for that OU

explain: Takeout availability — and which data types are allowed — can be restricted per OU.

stem: You need a single, whole-organization export of data for a one-time legal review, restricted to Super Admins. Which tool?
explain: The Data Export tool performs an org-wide export under Super Admin control; Takeout is per-user self-export.

stem: A regulated client requires covered data be stored at rest in Europe. What do you configure?

choices.text: A secondary domain hosted in the EU
A Vault export location in the EU
A Drive trust rule for EU users

explain: Data regions control where covered data is stored at rest; export location only affects where exports are produced.

stem: Your industry requires specific legal/compliance configurations across Workspace. Where do you primarily align these obligations?

choices.text: Across Vault retention/holds, DLP, data regions, and related compliance settings

explain: Regulatory alignment spans Vault, DLP, data regions, and related governance controls, not a single service.

stem: You want users to manually mark documents as “Public,” “Internal,” or “Confidential.” What feature provides this user classification?
explain: Classification labels let users (or automation) tag files; they can feed DLP and search.

stem: You’d like documents to be classified automatically using AI rather than relying on users. What capability supports this?
explain: AI classification can apply labels automatically based on content, reducing reliance on manual tagging.

stem: You want every new file in a Drive to start with a baseline classification unless changed. What do you set?
explain: A default classification applies a baseline label to files so nothing is left unclassified by accident.

stem: You want DLP to take action when a file carries the “Confidential” label. How do labels and DLP relate?

choices.text: DLP rules can use a classification label as a condition

explain: DLP can use the presence of a classification label as a condition to trigger actions.

stem: A user emptied Trash and needs a Doc they deleted yesterday. What’s the correct recovery path?

choices.text: Have an admin restore the user’s recently deleted Drive data within the recovery window

explain: Admins can restore recently deleted Drive (and Gmail) data within a limited window; Vault is for retention/eDiscovery, not user recovery.

stem: You apply a hold to only three custodians involved in a case, not the whole org. What scope does a Vault hold support?

choices.text: Specific accounts, or an OU/group, as needed

explain: Holds can target specific accounts or organizational units/groups relevant to a matter.

stem: A default retention rule says delete after one year, but a custom rule on Finance says keep for seven, and a hold also applies to one user. For that held Finance user, what governs?

choices.text: The data is deleted at one year
The hold (preservation) overrides deletion; the longer retention also applies

explain: Holds always prevent deletion; among retention rules, preservation/longer retention wins over shorter deletion.

stem: Counsel needs a defensible eDiscovery search spanning a custodian’s Gmail, Drive, and Chat. Which product is purpose-built?
explain: Vault is the eDiscovery and information-governance tool that searches across supported services and exports results.

stem: What is the key difference between Takeout and the Data Export tool?

choices.text: Takeout is per-user self-export; Data Export is an org-wide export run by Super Admins

explain: Takeout exports an individual user’s data; the Data Export tool exports the whole organization’s data under Super Admin control.

stem: You’re asked whether Vault counts as a backup solution. What’s the accurate statement?

choices.text: Yes, Vault is a backup product
No — Vault is for retention/eDiscovery, not operational backup/restore

explain: Vault preserves and discovers data for compliance/legal purposes; it isn’t a general backup-and-restore tool.

stem: You must prevent a specific data type (e.g., calendar data) from being included in user Takeout exports. How?

choices.text: Restrict the allowed data types in Takeout settings

explain: Takeout settings let you allow or restrict specific data types from being exported by users.

stem: DLP should warn but not block when an internal email contains a national ID number, logging the event for review. Which action set fits?

choices.text: Warn the user and audit/log the event

explain: DLP supports graduated actions; warning plus auditing fits a low-friction, monitored response to internal matches. Section 4 · Managing security policies & access controls (~20%)

stem: You’re enforcing 2-Step Verification org-wide and must avoid locking out users who haven’t registered a factor yet. What do you configure?

choices.text: An enrollment (grace) period and a new-user enrollment window before enforcement

explain: An enrollment grace period lets users register a second factor before enforcement begins, preventing lockouts.

stem: Which 2SV methods are the most phishing-resistant? (Choose TWO)
explain: Security keys and passkeys resist phishing; SMS is the weakest method and backup codes are only a fallback.

stem: The board mandates Workspace be reachable only from corporate-managed devices, regardless of who signs in. Which control fits best?

choices.text: Context-Aware Access with a device-based access level

explain: Context-Aware Access conditions access on attributes like device state, which is exactly a managed-device requirement.

stem: Users on shared kiosks should be signed out automatically after a short period. What do you configure?
explain: Google Session Control sets how long web sessions last before re-authentication, ideal for shared machines.

stem: A new help-desk hire should reset passwords and help users, but must not change security settings or billing. Which prebuilt role fits least privilege?
explain: Help Desk Admin is limited to password resets and basic user help — the least-privilege match.

stem: You need a role that grants only the privilege to manage groups and nothing else. What do you create or assign?

choices.text: Groups Admin (or a custom role with only group privileges)

explain: Use the prebuilt Groups Admin or a custom role scoped to just group management to follow least privilege.

stem: Which are Google-recommended practices for Super Admin accounts? (Choose TWO)

choices.text: Use them for routine daily administration
Keep the number of Super Admins small
Share one Super Admin account across the team
Protect them with the strongest 2SV, such as security keys

explain: Limit how many Super Admins exist and protect them with the strongest 2SV; don’t use them for daily work or share them.

stem: You want all users to have at least a 12-character password. Where do you set it?
explain: Minimum length and strength are set in the password management policy, scoped org-wide or per OU.

stem: After a suspected breach, you must force all users in an OU to set new passwords at next sign-in. What do you do?

choices.text: Require password change at next sign-in for that OU

explain: You can require a password change at next sign-in for selected users/OUs to rotate credentials quickly.

stem: Leadership wants a single page that flags weak security configurations and recommends fixes. Where do you look?

choices.text: The security health page in the security center

explain: The security health page highlights configuration gaps against recommended settings.

stem: A phishing email reached many inboxes and you must find and delete copies and suspend affected users. Which tool?
explain: The investigation tool searches across mailboxes and can take remediation actions like deleting messages and suspending users.

stem: You want an at-a-glance overview of security posture and trends across the org. Which feature provides it?
explain: The security dashboard summarizes posture and trends; the investigation tool drills into specific incidents.

stem: You want an automatic alert and optional action whenever a large number of files are shared externally in a short time. What do you create?

choices.text: An activity rule/alert (in the investigation tool / alert center)

explain: Activity rules can trigger alerts and automated actions when defined conditions occur.

stem: Where do admins receive and triage notifications about potential security and configuration issues?
explain: The alert center centralizes notifications (e.g., suspicious activity, system alerts) for triage.

stem: You want to limit which third-party Marketplace apps users can install to an approved set. What do you configure?

choices.text: The Marketplace allowlist (allow only approved apps)

explain: The Marketplace allowlist restricts installation to apps you’ve approved.

stem: A risky OAuth app requests broad Gmail and Drive scopes. You want to mark it Blocked and stop it from accessing those scopes. What do you use?

choices.text: API controls / app access control (classify app as Blocked, restrict sensitive scopes)

explain: App access control (API controls) classifies apps as Trusted/Limited/Blocked and restricts access to sensitive scopes.

stem: In app access control, how can you classify connected third-party apps?
explain: Apps can be set Trusted, Limited, or Blocked, governing their access to Google services and scopes.

stem: Your company uses a third-party SaaS app and wants Workspace credentials to sign users in. In this SSO setup, Workspace acts as what?

choices.text: The identity provider (IdP) for the SaaS app

explain: When configuring SSO for third-party apps, Workspace can act as the IdP that authenticates users into those apps.

stem: Only the Media OU should have access to the additional Google service YouTube; others shouldn’t. How do you scope it?

choices.text: Enable the additional service (YouTube) for the Media OU only

explain: Access to additional Google services like YouTube can be enabled per OU.

stem: After offboarding a vendor, you must revoke all the OAuth tokens their app held to your data. What do you do?

choices.text: Remove the connected app/sites and revoke its access in app access control

explain: Removing connected apps revokes their granted OAuth access to organization data.

stem: You want a context-aware policy applied to a security group rather than an entire OU. Is that supported?

choices.text: Yes, access levels/policies can target groups as well as OUs

explain: Security policies, including context-aware access, can be applied to groups in addition to OUs.

stem: You enforce 2SV but need a brief window for brand-new hires to enroll before they’re blocked. Which setting addresses just new users?
explain: A new-user enrollment period gives newly created accounts time to register a second factor before enforcement.

stem: A regular (non-admin) user forgot their password and has no recovery set. What’s the standard remedy?

choices.text: An admin resets their password in the Admin console

explain: For ordinary users, an admin can reset the password directly; self-recovery requires recovery options being configured.

stem: You want to require the strongest 2SV (security keys) only for admins, while other users may use the Authenticator app. How?

choices.text: Apply a 2SV policy requiring security keys to the admins’ group/OU

explain: 2SV enforcement can be scoped, so you can require security keys for admins while allowing other methods elsewhere.

stem: A managed Android fleet should only run an approved set of apps from Google Play. Where do you control this?

choices.text: Managed Google Play app management (allow/block apps) for the OU

explain: Managed Google Play lets you allow, block, or push approved apps to managed Android devices.

stem: You want the Marketplace to operate in “allow only what I approve” mode rather than letting users install anything. Which mode?
explain: Allowlist mode restricts installs to the apps you’ve explicitly approved.

stem: Sign-ins from outside approved countries should be blocked for an OU. Which mechanism expresses this best?

choices.text: A context-aware access level based on IP/geography (with login controls)

explain: Context-aware access levels can include IP/geography attributes to restrict where sign-ins are allowed.

stem: You receive an alert that a user downloaded an unusually large volume of files. Where do you investigate the details and act?

choices.text: The security investigation tool (with relevant log events)

explain: The investigation tool lets you query log events (e.g., Drive) and take remediation actions on findings.

stem: Leadership wants admin privileges split so one team manages users and another manages groups, with no overlap. What’s the approach?

choices.text: Assign least-privilege roles: User Management Admin to one, Groups Admin to the other

explain: Prebuilt scoped roles (User Management Admin, Groups Admin) cleanly separate duties under least privilege.

stem: You must delegate help-desk powers but only for users within one regional OU. How do you scope a custom role?

choices.text: Roles can’t be scoped to an OU
Assign the role with an organizational-unit scope so it applies only to that OU

explain: Administrative roles can be assigned with an org-unit scope, limiting the admin’s authority to that OU.

stem: Which security center component is best for identifying current threats and risks across the org, such as exposed files or risky devices?

choices.text: The security dashboard/health and investigation tools in the security center

explain: The security center (dashboard, health page, and investigation tool) surfaces threats and risks and supports remediation.

stem: A compromised account is actively sending spam. Using the investigation tool, what’s an appropriate immediate action?

choices.text: Suspend the account and delete the malicious messages

explain: The investigation tool can suspend the account and remove malicious messages to contain the incident.

stem: You want to ensure that even valid passwords don’t grant access from unmanaged devices for the Finance group. Which combination is strongest?

choices.text: 2SV plus a context-aware access level requiring a managed device

explain: Pairing 2SV with context-aware access (managed-device requirement) protects access even if a password is known.

stem: You need a record of administrative changes (who changed a setting and when) to investigate a misconfiguration. Which log?
explain: Admin-console setting changes are recorded in the admin audit log.

stem: You want users to be able to recover their own accounts via a verification code to a recovery phone/email. What must be configured?

choices.text: Account recovery options (recovery phone/email) and the policy allowing self-recovery

explain: Self-recovery depends on recovery options being set and the org policy permitting user account recovery.

stem: You discover a third-party add-on with access to user mail that should never have been approved. Beyond blocking it, what limits future risk?

choices.text: Set sensitive scopes to require trusted apps and run the Marketplace in allowlist mode

explain: Restricting sensitive scopes to trusted apps and allowlisting the Marketplace prevents unapproved apps from gaining access.

stem: Which prebuilt role would let someone manage user accounts (create, suspend, reset) without granting security or billing control?
explain: User Management Admin handles user lifecycle tasks without broad security/billing privileges.

stem: You want to be alerted whenever a Super Admin role is granted to any account. What’s the best mechanism?

choices.text: An alert/activity rule (admin privilege change) in the alert center / rules

explain: Activity rules/alerts can notify admins when sensitive events like admin-role grants occur.

stem: To reduce risk from stale sessions, you want browser sessions for web apps to require re-auth daily for a sensitive OU. What do you set?

choices.text: Google Session Control session length for that OU

explain: Session Control sets web session duration before re-authentication, scoped per OU.

stem: A user is repeatedly prompted with extra verification when signing in from new locations, and asks why. What is this protection called?
explain: Login challenges add verification steps for risky or unfamiliar sign-ins to help block unauthorized access. Section 5 · Managing browsers & endpoints (~10%)

stem: An employee leaves and returns their personal phone that held the corporate account. You must remove company data but leave personal content untouched. What do you do?

choices.text: Block the device from the network

explain: For BYOD, an account wipe removes only corporate data; a full device wipe is for company-owned hardware.

stem: You want to require screen locks and be able to wipe corporate data from personal phones with minimal setup and no agent installed. Which management level?
explain: Basic mobile management is agentless, on by default, and supports screen-lock enforcement and account wipe.

stem: You need device approval and full device wipe on company-owned phones, plus app management. Which level (edition permitting)?
explain: Advanced mobile management adds device approval, stronger policies, app management, and full device wipe.

stem: You must force-install a specific Chrome extension for the Finance OU only. Where do you do this?

choices.text: Devices > Chrome > Apps & extensions, scoped to the Finance OU

explain: Chrome extension policies (force-install/allow/block) are set under Chrome Apps & extensions and scoped by OU/group.

stem: Before you can apply Chrome browser policies centrally, what must you do first?

choices.text: Enroll the browsers using an enrollment token (Chrome Browser Cloud Management)

explain: Browsers must be enrolled into Chrome Browser Cloud Management via an enrollment token before policies apply.

stem: A managed device is lost. You need to remove all data from it remotely. For a company-owned device, what action applies?
explain: For company-owned hardware, a full device wipe (factory reset) removes all data.

stem: You want to block a known-malicious Chrome extension across the company. Where?

choices.text: Chrome Apps & extensions policy set to block that extension

explain: Extensions can be set to blocked org-wide (or per OU) under Chrome Apps & extensions.

stem: You must ensure managed Chrome browsers install updates automatically and stay current. Which policy area?
explain: Chrome update policies control how/when managed browsers receive updates.

stem: Field laptops need Chrome apps available offline. Which setting addresses this?

choices.text: Chrome offline-access policy for the relevant apps

explain: Chrome policies can enable offline access for supported apps on managed browsers.

stem: What is Chrome Browser Cloud Management primarily used for?

choices.text: Centrally enrolling and managing Chrome browser policies and extensions

explain: Chrome Browser Cloud Management centrally enforces browser policies and manages extensions across enrolled browsers.

stem: You need an inventory of all registered mobile devices, both company-owned and BYOD, with their status. Where do you look?

choices.text: The Devices (endpoints) section of the Admin console

explain: The Devices/endpoints area lists registered devices and their management status for visibility and control.

stem: BYOD users must set a screen lock before accessing corporate mail on mobile. Which management approach is the minimum that achieves this?

choices.text: Basic mobile management with a screen-lock requirement

explain: Basic mobile management can require a screen lock on personal devices without installing an agent.

stem: Company-owned devices must be approved by an admin before they can access data. Which level supports device approval?
explain: Device approval (admin must approve before access) is an Advanced mobile management capability.

stem: You want to allow only an approved list of Chrome extensions and block everything else for an OU. Which configuration?

choices.text: Set the extension policy to allow only the listed extensions (block all others)

explain: You can restrict installs to an allowlist of approved extensions while blocking the rest, scoped by OU.

stem: A complex device scenario needs capabilities Google’s built-in management doesn’t cover. What’s the option?
explain: When requirements exceed basic/advanced features, a third-party MDM can be integrated.

stem: An employee’s company-owned phone needs to be re-purposed for a new hire. What’s the correct offboarding step?

choices.text: Device wipe (factory reset) to remove all data before reassignment

explain: For reassigning company-owned hardware, a full device wipe clears all data prior to the new user.

stem: You want to push a managed configuration and force-install line-of-business apps on company Android devices. Which combination?

choices.text: Advanced mobile management with managed Google Play app deployment

explain: Advanced management plus managed Google Play lets you push configurations and force-install approved apps.

stem: You need to confirm which Chrome browsers are enrolled and what policies they received. Where do you check?

choices.text: The managed browsers list under Devices > Chrome

explain: The managed browsers view shows enrolled browsers, their OU, and applied policies.

stem: A device shows as registered but isn’t receiving the mobile policy you set. What’s a common first check?

choices.text: Confirm the device is in the correct OU/group the policy targets and is approved/synced

explain: Policies apply by OU/group and require the device to be approved and synced; verify targeting and status first.

stem: To manage Chrome policies for devices that aren’t signed into a managed profile, what’s the right mechanism?

choices.text: Enroll the browser itself (Chrome Browser Cloud Management) so device-level policies apply

explain: Enrolling the browser applies policies at the browser/device level, independent of the signed-in user. Section 6 · Monitoring & troubleshooting (~13%)

stem: Multiple users report Gmail is down. What’s your first check to see whether it’s a Google-side outage?
explain: The Status Dashboard shows known service disruptions — the right first stop for “is it down for everyone?”

stem: A user says an email expected two days ago never arrived. What’s the most direct tool to trace its delivery?
explain: Email Log Search traces a specific message’s delivery path and status within the retention window.

stem: An email failed authentication and you want to inspect its SPF/DKIM/DMARC results from the raw header. Which tool?
explain: The Messageheader tool in the Admin Toolbox parses a raw header and shows authentication results.

stem: Google Support asks for a network capture of a failing web request in Chrome. What do you provide?

choices.text: A HAR file captured from Chrome DevTools

explain: A HAR file (DevTools > Network > preserve log > reproduce > save as HAR) captures the network exchange; treat it as sensitive.

stem: Users complain of poor audio and video in Meet calls. Which tool helps diagnose network/quality issues?
explain: The Meet quality tool surfaces network and media-quality data to diagnose A/V problems.

stem: You need to find who changed a Drive sharing setting in the Admin console last week. Which log?
explain: Admin-console setting changes are recorded in the admin audit log; Drive log events show user file activity, not console settings.

stem: You want to review recent sign-in activity and failed logins for a user suspected of compromise. Which log?
explain: The login audit log records authentication events such as sign-ins and failed attempts.

stem: A user deleted an important Gmail message and emptied Trash yesterday. What’s the recovery path?

choices.text: An admin can restore the user’s recently deleted Gmail data within the recovery window

explain: Admins can restore recently deleted Gmail/Drive data within a limited window via the Admin console.

stem: Drive for desktop won’t sync on a user’s laptop. What’s a reasonable first troubleshooting step?

choices.text: Check connectivity/sign-in, then restart or reinstall Drive for desktop and review sync errors

explain: Common Drive for desktop fixes include verifying sign-in/connectivity and restarting or reinstalling the client.

stem: A user’s events stopped syncing to Outlook. What’s a likely area to investigate?

choices.text: The Calendar sync/connector setup for Outlook (e.g., GWSMO) and account re-sync

explain: Outlook calendar sync relies on the connector (GWSMO) and account configuration; re-sync or reconfigure to fix.

stem: Colleagues can’t see a user’s free/busy when scheduling. What’s the most likely cause?

choices.text: Calendar sharing settings limiting free/busy visibility

explain: Free/busy visibility is governed by Calendar sharing settings; restrictive defaults hide availability.

stem: A user reports a forwarding filter isn’t moving messages as expected. Where do you start?

choices.text: Review the user’s Gmail filters/forwarding settings (and any admin forwarding restrictions)

explain: Forwarding/filter issues are usually in the user’s Gmail filter rules or an org policy restricting forwarding.

stem: Leadership wants to track storage consumption across the organization over time. Where do you find this?

choices.text: Reports (usage/storage reports) in the Admin console

explain: Admin reports include storage and usage metrics for monitoring consumption.

stem: You want to see which apps are most used and track adoption across teams. Which area?
explain: Usage and adoption reports show app activity and engagement across the organization.

stem: You need to monitor device activity, such as new registrations and policy events. Where do you look?

choices.text: Device activity reports / the Devices section

explain: Device activity is available through device reports and the endpoints (Devices) area.

stem: Before a planned change, you want to know about upcoming Workspace feature releases. Which resource?

choices.text: The Google Workspace updates blog and release calendar

explain: The Workspace updates blog and release calendar announce upcoming and current feature releases.

stem: You’re opening a case with Google Support for an intermittent web error. Which Google-recommended step strengthens the case?

choices.text: Document repro steps and attach appropriate logs/HAR files

explain: Documenting reproduction steps and attaching relevant logs/HAR files helps Support diagnose efficiently.

stem: A message bounced with a delivery error. Using Email Log Search, what can you determine?

choices.text: The delivery status, recipient response, and reason the message failed

explain: Email Log Search reveals delivery status and the SMTP response/reason, helping pinpoint why a message failed.

stem: A legitimate newsletter is being filtered as spam for many users. What’s an appropriate admin remedy?

choices.text: Allowlist the sender or adjust spam policy after confirming via Email Log Search

explain: Confirm the pattern via ELS, then allowlist the sender or tune spam settings rather than disabling protection.

stem: You need to determine who shared a specific Drive file externally and when. Which source?

choices.text: Drive log events (audit) in the investigation/reporting tools

explain: Drive log events record file and sharing activity by users, ideal for tracing who shared a file.

stem: A user can edit a shared Doc but a teammate can only view it, and they expect equal access. What’s the likely cause?

choices.text: The file/folder sharing permissions differ for the two users

explain: Differing access usually reflects per-user/role permissions on the file or its parent; check and align sharing settings.

stem: Some users can’t access a scheduled Meet event. What’s a sensible first check?

choices.text: Whether Meet is enabled for their OU and the meeting’s access/safety settings

explain: Meet access problems often trace to OU-level Meet enablement or the meeting’s join/safety settings.

stem: To investigate a pattern of unusual activity across services, you want to correlate log events and optionally act. Which tool combines search and remediation?
explain: The investigation tool queries multiple log sources and can take remediation actions on findings.

stem: A user reports a service is failing only for them, but the Status Dashboard shows all green. What’s the best next step?

choices.text: Gather repro steps and relevant logs (e.g., HAR, audit logs) to isolate the user-specific issue
Disable the service for everyone Answer key & explanations Don't peek until you've finished. Each entry gives the correct answer and a short why.

explain: A green dashboard points to a local/user-specific problem; collect repro steps and logs to isolate it before escalating.
